data.gender_notes: Venustina is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Latin word venustus meaning beautiful, graceful, and charming. In Christianity, this name is derived from various female saints named Venus or Venusta. The name Venustina carries the meaning “Beautiful, Gracious” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Venustina usually hope their child will grow to embody beautiful, gracious and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolic of God's grace and beauty.

She is said to have been a beautiful young woman who converted many to Christianity through her witness and good works. According to legend, she was captured, tortured, and ultimately beheaded for her faith. Her feast day is celebrated on January 15th.

Another Venustina, a 16th century Italian saint, is believed to have been born in the town of Spoleto. She was a laywoman who devoted her life to caring for the sick and the poor. Her acts of charity and compassion earned her the nickname 'Venustina', meaning 'graceful' or 'pleasing'. She is also said to have had a miraculous encounter with St. Francis of Assisi.
